subject: Information Theory
title: Network Capacity
description: A short lesson to help you apply Network Capacity.

hook.text: A single fiber optic cable carries 70 terabits per second. Shannon's limit tells us exactly how much more is possible.

buildup.text: Each link in a network has a channel capacity. The network's total throughput depends on topology and routing.

discovery.text: The max-flow min-cut theorem: a network's maximum information flow equals its minimum bottleneck capacity.

twist.text: Adding links doesn't always help. Braess's paradox shows that extra capacity can actually reduce flow in some networks.

climax.text: Network information theory extends Shannon's point-to-point results to multi-node systems—and many problems remain open.

punchline.text: The weakest link limits the whole network. Bottlenecks rule.

quiz.question: What does the max-flow min-cut theorem state?
options: Maximum flow equals the minimum bottleneck cut capacity
Flow is unlimited in large networks
